items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: I heard this Ike Dixon and Ford Dabney then Fletcher Henderson come down and shook everybody up

ctx.x: And so around about 8 or 9, I was living on Virginia Avenue and George Washington Circle, (unintelligible) and she sent me to get some clothes to be washed, and on the way there was a dancing place, called it Jordan St. Mark's and I heard -- the first time -- I heard a little bit of piano playing, but I heard the violin and I was enchanted by this. I said, oh, what is that! And then I lingered a little too long and Mama was wondering what happened and why are you so late. so I said, what's that, and she said oh,…

was People of Color and later I think it was Ford Dabney's band. They had big _____phones and the people they were beautiful, (unintelligible) and so that was it and my mother and my family, they would sing. Now, these people, they wasn't too strong on education, but they was singing solfeggio--- do-re-mi-fa-so-la-ti-do; they were singing and (unintelligible) so then what--
What kind of songs were they singing.
